doc: A stored API key remembers which origin it was entered for (the binding; the key itself is never part of it). Before a stored key is used for `destination` the binding is classified, and every state has ONE defined outcome, so 'no record' and 'could not read the records' can never be mistaken for each other.

states.BOUND_MATCH: a binding exists and equals the destination -> send
states.BOUND_MISMATCH: a binding exists and differs from the destination -> refuse (KeyRouteError), nothing is sent
states.LEGACY_UNBOUND: no binding record for this key (config readable) -> refuse (KeyRouteError), nothing is sent. Retired as a send state in S3.1: a key whose destination cannot be proven is never sent. Every key the app stores is encrypted and bound in the same atomic write; a legacy plaintext key is imported, bound, verified and only then deleted; if that migration has not completed the plaintext is kept (never destroyed) and reported but not used, and a key supplied only through the process environment has no binding either. The state is kept as a name for the record, not as a way to send
states.BINDING_UNAVAILABLE: the binding records cannot be read (config unreadable or corrupt) -> refuse, nothing is sent

platforms.android: not applicable: keys are stored per route and only lent between same-origin routes (see origin.json same_origin_cases)
